 Follow Radiation testing results spark additional fear and anger
 Dave McKinley Sat, November 7, 2026 at 12:43 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Several Niagara County residents have gotten additional results back from radiation and chemical tests taken on their property and the news is not good ... leaving them fearful for their families and angry at a government that they say is not moving quickly nor doing nearly enough to help them.
 Affected homeowners received the results Thursday night, and by Friday they were still reeling over their worst fears having materialized.
 They used adjectives such as heartbroken, sad, and horrified to describe their feelings.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It's overwhelming," said Carrie Webber of Liberty Avenue in the Town of Niagara.
 A radiation expert who reviewed the testing results says they have good reason to feel that way.
 "The materials represent several types of hazards," said Michael Ketterer, a retired chemistry professor from the University of Northern Arizona and a native of North Tonawanda.
 According to Ketterer, the levels of radiation shown in some samples — which likely stemmed from industrial dumping conducted decades ago — are high enough to be a threat to human health.
 "People need to be kept away from this radioactive sand material, and this sand material needs to be kept apart from people," he said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Meanwhile, life for the McKiernan family — whose home near Love Canal is suspected of being chemically contaminated — has gone from bad to worse after learning the school their son attends, Catholic Academy on Military Road, has now been identified as a place of concern and will be tested for radiation next week.
 According to Jocelyn McKiernan, when she went to the the school on Friday seeking more information, she was thwarted by a security guard who escorted her from the building.
 "I was demoralized today by the security guard in front of our son, other parents, children, and staff," she said.
 Innocent but feeling guilty 
 None of the property owners put the hazardous materials on their land, nor were any of them aware of its presence when they moved in.
 Advertisement Advertisement That makes another common feeling among them both surprising, and heartbreaking to hear.
 "I didn't know what was there but I can't begin to describe the guilt that I have," said Lexi Hawk of Fox Avenue. "My job as a parent is to protect my child, and I guess we didn't do that, and now we have to be terrified for her future."
 "I too feel enormous guilt for moving my family into this house," said Carolyn Johnson, who lives up the street from Hawk.
 "What did I let my children be born into?" Webber asked. "There's no words you can bring to the table to explain the fear and the unknown in this situation."
 Advertisement Advertisement Their fear, however, has turned to anger over a government they say has been non-responsive to their needs.
 Calling on Hochul to do something 
 "I want our government and our governor, Kathy Hochul, to stand beside us and be a strong voice in backing our community," Hawk said.
 Added Rev. Merle Showers, a retired Methodist minister now actively involved in environmental causes, "I am so ashamed of my government and my governor."
 Anne Rabe, Former NYPIRG Environmental Policy Director and currently a member of Don't Waste NY, said it was egregious that landowners are being notified only now of the test results.
 Advertisement Advertisement "The test results they received, two days after election day, from tests done in July, show alarming and excessive levels of radioactive chemicals," she said.
 Rabe lent her voice to a chorus of others saying the situation warrants an emergency declaration on the part of the state and federal governments in order to utilize the Superfund for remediation and relocation where necessary.
